decision: Use a single data layer contract for all public and admin events.
implementation_spec: All components push normalized event objects with event name, page type, language, canonical owner, and surface id.
why_this_way: One contract prevents double-tagging and inconsistent reports.
acceptance_gate: Every event in analytics-event-dictionary.csv has one trigger and one payload schema.

decision: Use Google recommended events where they fit: search, view_search_results, view_item_list, select_item, view_item, generate_lead.
implementation_spec: Map NadLan project/property behaviors into recommended events only when the meaning is accurate.
why_this_way: Recommended events improve standard reporting; misuse creates bad data.
acceptance_gate: Each recommended event has required parameters and a visible QA proof.

decision: Use custom events for NadLan-specific behavior: unit_select, showroom_open, map_poi_select, contractor_intake_submit, publish_gate_block.
implementation_spec: Custom events keep product-specific actions measurable without forcing them into the wrong Google event.
why_this_way: NadLan has showroom and contractor behaviors that standard ecommerce does not describe well.
acceptance_gate: Custom events appear in DebugView with required parameters and no personal data.

decision: Create approved event parameters and register reportable custom dimensions only for values the owner will use.
implementation_spec: Core parameters: page_type, language, project_id, unit_id, city, asset_status, lead_type, source_surface, canonical_owner.
why_this_way: Too many dimensions create clutter; too few make the funnel impossible to read.
acceptance_gate: Each dashboard card lists the parameters it depends on.

decision: Never send names, phone numbers, emails, message body, exact private address, or raw sensitive financial values to analytics.
implementation_spec: Use internal ids, bands, categories, and CRM record references instead of personal values.
why_this_way: The site can measure business value without leaking personal data.
acceptance_gate: Privacy scan confirms no personal form fields are pushed to analytics.

decision: Every lead gets source surface, page type, project id if present, unit id if present, language, lead type, and CRM id.
implementation_spec: Analytics stores event context; CRM/form system stores the contact record.
why_this_way: This lets NadLan prove value to developers and professionals without mixing contact data into analytics.
acceptance_gate: Submitted lead has analytics event, CRM record, and thank-you screenshot.

decision: Measure showroom entry, unit selection, view layer, tour open, consultation request, lead start, and lead submit.
implementation_spec: Each step must include asset status so fake or missing assets do not inflate contractor claims.
why_this_way: Contractors need proof of engagement, but proof must distinguish real assets from presentation states.
acceptance_gate: Dashboard shows showroom funnel by project, language, and asset status.

decision: Measure search, result list view, filter, sort, card open, save, compare, contact click, and lead submit.
implementation_spec: Keep route, filter, and sort events stable before adding advanced reports.
why_this_way: This proves whether the premium search and card system creates intent.
acceptance_gate: Dashboard shows result-to-detail and detail-to-lead rates.

decision: Measure language switch, English route opens, foreign-buyer guide engagement, concierge form start, and concierge submit.
implementation_spec: Segment by language and country page once pages exist.
why_this_way: Foreign investor value is a strategic revenue line and must not be guessed.
acceptance_gate: Dashboard shows foreign-buyer traffic, engaged sessions, and leads by language.

decision: Measure contractor intake start, package interest, asset bundle state, submission, follow-up status, and closed revenue outside analytics.
implementation_spec: Analytics measures behavior; CRM tracks actual sales stages and revenue.
why_this_way: The owner needs a contractor sales cockpit, not vanity clicks.
acceptance_gate: Owner dashboard distinguishes inquiry, qualified lead, proposal, won, and lost.

decision: Build the owner dashboard from real sources only: GA4/GSC/CRM/admin registry and screenshot evidence.
implementation_spec: Cards: traffic by page group, lead funnel, showroom funnel, property intent, international leads, professional leads, contractor pipeline, content gate health.
why_this_way: No invented values or screenshots of empty dashboards as proof.
acceptance_gate: Every card displays source, last updated date, and missing-data state.

decision: Do not call tracking complete until Tag Assistant or DebugView evidence exists for each P0 event.
implementation_spec: Capture event firing screenshots and payload notes for desktop and mobile routes.
why_this_way: Events that are not debugged will create false confidence.
acceptance_gate: P0 event screenshots are saved and linked from evidence register.

decision: Implement consent-aware tagging before marketing or remarketing use.
implementation_spec: Consent state must be initialized before tags that depend on consent.
why_this_way: Tracking must respect user choices and avoid legal shortcuts.
acceptance_gate: Consent mode is visible in debug evidence and reviewed before marketing pixels expand.

decision: Every visual release adds or updates analytics coverage notes.
implementation_spec: If a page adds CTA, form, map, showroom, calculator, or contractor action, the event dictionary must be updated in the same build slice.
why_this_way: The event dictionary stays alive instead of becoming stale documentation.
acceptance_gate: PR or release note names added/changed events and screenshots.
